rows.title: Movie Theaters Sue New Jersey For Right To Reopen
rows.standfirst: Movie chains, including AMC Entertainment, Cinemark and Regal Cinemas, are seeking an injunction against Gov. Philip Murphy's phased reopening schedule unless it allows them to reopen.

rows.title: Live Music Industry Blues
rows.standfirst: Live music events are like micro-economies that support hundreds of small businesses. Coronavirus is hammering them.

rows.title: CFPB Strips Some Consumer Protections For Payday Loans
rows.standfirst: Federal regulators issue a new rule that removes a key provision crafted during the Obama administration. Lenders no longer have to check that borrowers can repay a loan.

rows.title: Opinion: Companies Have A Duty To Defend Democracy
rows.standfirst: A survey of 50 former U.S. ambassadors shows they believe democracy and elections are the top issues that companies need to prepare to publicly address.

rows.title: What Beer Sales Tell Us About The Recession
rows.standfirst: Cheap beer sales are surging but are still losing ground to craft beer. Yet craft breweries are still suffering. What is going on?

rows.title: Boston Tavern Pivots To 'Plan B' To Try To Survive The Pandemic
rows.standfirst: Cornwall's has been a Kenmore Square mainstay for more than four decades. Now it's preparing to reopen — and to reinvent itself for survival during the pandemic.

rows.title: 'Almost In Tears': A Hairstylist Worries About Reopening Too Soon
rows.standfirst: NPR's Chris Arnold sits down in the barber's chair as his 65-year-old hairstylist tells him about working 13-hour days, as he worries about catching the coronavirus.

rows.title: As Americans Avoided Restaurants And Doctors' Offices, Those Businesses Got Loans
rows.standfirst: The small business sectors that received the largest share of federal loans from the coronavirus relief package known as PPP include restaurants, doctors' offices, car dealerships and law firms.

rows.title: Uber Gobbles Up Postmates In $2.65 Billion Bet On Food Delivery
rows.standfirst: The deal is a sign of how the coronavirus pandemic has turned Uber's business model upside down, with customers shunning ride-hailing and flocking to delivery services.

rows.title: Unintended Consequences, Hidden Deaths
rows.standfirst: The way organizations and governments respond to disasters often have hidden consequences; sometimes those consequences can be fatal.

rows.title: 'We Need Help': People At Higher Coronavirus Risk Fear Losing Federal Unemployment
rows.standfirst: An extra $600 a week in federal unemployment runs out at the end of July — even for people with underlying health conditions who are at much greater risk if they contract COVID-19.

rows.title: Court Rules Dakota Access Pipeline Must Be Emptied For Now
rows.standfirst: A federal judge has ordered the Army Corps of Engineers to produce a full environmental review. Until then, oil must stop flowing through the controversial pipeline.

rows.title: Early Coronavirus Testing Restrictions Led To Some Big ER Bills
rows.standfirst: People with COVID-19 symptoms in March and April were often billed for expensive scans and bloodwork because they didn't qualify back then for a confirmatory coronavirus test. Some are crying foul.

rows.title: Social Entrepreneurs: Taking On World Problems
rows.standfirst: The past decade or so has seen explosive growth in the number of social entrepreneurs — innovators who take a business-like approach to solving social problems. NPR profiles some of these entrepreneurs.

rows.title: Inside Seating? A Harlem Bar Owner Navigates COVID-19's Changing Rules
rows.standfirst: 67 Orange Street makes do with take-out and outdoor service while waiting for a decision on inside dining in NYC.

rows.title: Coronavirus Costs Delta Air Lines Nearly $6 Billion In 2nd Quarter
rows.standfirst: A sharp drop in air travel due to the pandemic cuts into Delta's bottom line, but the airline says it will continue to block out middle seats to create more distance between passengers.

rows.title: Oil Storage Wars
rows.standfirst: Because of the global economic slowdown, there's a glut of oil on the market right now. And companies are coming up with creative ways to store it.

rows.title: In Reversal, U.K. Will Ban Huawei Equipment From Its 5G Network
rows.standfirst: British regulators say they had little choice after the U.S. imposed sanctions that could affect the viability of Huawei products. Existing 5G equipment must be removed from the network by 2027.

rows.title: Stay-At-Home Improvement: DIY Builders Help Drive Up Lumber Prices
rows.standfirst: With summer travel plans on hold because of the pandemic, a lot of Americans are putting money into projects around the house. That's taxing lumber supplies and pushing prices higher.

rows.title: How Absentee Landowners Keep Farmers From Protecting Water And Soil
rows.standfirst: America's vast fields of corn and soybeans have displaced wildlife and polluted waterways. Farmers could help solve those problems, but often don't, in part because they rent that land.

rows.title: 'We Still Face Much Uncertainty': Pandemic Hammers Big Banks
rows.standfirst: The dramatic collapse of the U.S. economy is pummeling America's largest banks. Wells Fargo has posted its first quarterly loss since 2008 and JPMorgan Chase has set aside billions to cover bad loans.

rows.title: Getting Out Of Medical Debt Can Feel Impossible. Here's How To Do It
rows.standfirst: One in five Americans struggles with medical bills. The secret is that there's something you can do about it — you just have to know where to look and how to ask.

rows.title: Is It Time To Kill The Penny?
rows.standfirst: As America experiences a coin shortage, Planet Money takes a look at the value of the penny.

rows.title: The Customer Is Always Right. Except When They Won't Wear A Mask
rows.standfirst: In the age of COVID-19, most people follow social distancing and mask guidelines when they enter stores and restaurants. But then there are the nightmare customers who won't comply.

rows.title: California Closes Indoor Businesses Statewide As COVID-19 Cases Surge
rows.standfirst: Restaurants, movie theaters and museums are among the businesses required to suspend their indoor operations statewide under Gov. Gavin Newsom's Monday announcement. Bars must close entirely.

rows.title: Schools, Businesses, Cities Push Back On Rule Blocking Some International Students
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration says it will ban international students in the fall if their education is online-only. Colleges and businesses say that decision could devastate the economy.

rows.title: Leaving Prison In The COVID-19 Economy
rows.standfirst: Reentering the world and the workforce after you've been in prison is hard enough at the best of times. The coronavirus pandemic has made it a whole lot harder.

rows.title: Red Ink Overflowing: In June, U.S. Borrowed A Typical Year's Worth
rows.standfirst: The federal deficit is ballooning as the government tries to cushion the blow from the coronavirus pandemic. June's shortfall totals $864 billion — more than in an entire typical year.

rows.title: Fresh Scrutiny For Fox's Tucker Carlson As Top Writer Quits Over Bigoted Posts
rows.standfirst: A top writer for Fox News' Tucker Carlson resigns after CNN revealed his racist and sexist posts, reviving criticism of Carlson's commentaries. Carlson is set to address the controversy Monday.

rows.title: The Racial Justice Reckoning Over Sports Team Names Is Spreading
rows.standfirst: In the wake of George Floyd's killing, Confederate monuments have fallen, food companies have scrubbed racist imagery from labels, and now, pro sports teams names are under fresh review.

rows.title: Un-HolyLand? An Arab Muslim Reckoning With Racism
rows.standfirst: After his daughter's racist and anti-LGBTQ social media posts became public, an Arab-Muslim entrepreneur is fighting to keep his once-burgeoning business alive in the middle of a national — and personal — reckoning with anti-blackness.

rows.title: Twitter Removes Thousands Of QAnon Accounts, Promises Sweeping Ban On The Conspiracy
rows.standfirst: Twitter has removed more than 7,000 accounts associated with QAnon as part of a broad-based crackdown on the pro-Trump conspiracy theory. Twitter says QAnon postings have led to real-world harm.

rows.title: FAA Inches Closer To Approving Boeing's Fixes To Troubled 737 Max
rows.standfirst: The FAA says an airworthiness directive for Boeing's 737 Max is near, but it still may be months before the troubled plane flies passengers again.

rows.title: A Tale Of Two Camdens
rows.standfirst: The city of Camden, New Jersey is cited as an example of how cities can change their approach to policing. But the story of Camden and its cops isn't a simple one.

rows.title: It 'Looks Very Scary For Renters' As Federal Eviction Relief Expiration Nears
rows.standfirst: NPR's Noel King speaks with Matt Desmond, founder of Princeton's Eviction Lab, about the threat of a rising number of evictions nationwide as federal evictions relief draws to an end.

rows.title: Record Low Mortgage Rates Put More Cash In Pockets, But May Not Boost Economy Much
rows.standfirst: A historic drop in rates has millions of homeowners refinancing to save money. It's helping home sales, but it's not helping the broader economy as much as it would in a normal recession.

rows.title: Seeking Suburban Votes, Trump To Repeal Rule Combating Racial Bias In Housing
rows.standfirst: The president has been talking a lot about suburbs lately, in particular about an Obama-era rule to limit housing discrimination. It appears to be a fear-based tactic to win swing voters.

rows.title: Independent Venues Face Bleak Future Without Aid
rows.standfirst: Small music venues in the US are looking for a lifeline — and a new bill in Congress called the Restart Act might be it. Advocates say the future of independent clubs relies on government relief.

rows.title: Restaurants' 'Existential Crisis'
rows.standfirst: Restaurants are getting squeezed. How many will survive? And what should we do about it?

rows.title: EU Agrees To $858 Billion In Grants, Loans To Bail Out Pandemic-Battered Economies
rows.standfirst: Exhausted leaders emerged from a marathon five days of talks with a rescue package to help member states weather their worst economic downturn since the Great Depression.

rows.title: Civil Suit Against Former Fox News Anchor Ed Henry Alleges Rape, Sexual Misconduct
rows.standfirst: The suit was filed in federal court in Manhattan by two former Fox News employees. Fox hosts Tucker Carlson and Sean Hannity are also named and accused of sexual misconduct.

rows.title: Essential Workers Hold Walkouts And Protests In National 'Strike For Black Lives'
rows.standfirst: Front-line workers in several U.S. cities walked off their jobs and took to the streets to demand racial and economic justice.

rows.title: This Weekend's (Fiscal) Cliffhanger
rows.standfirst: Unless Congress acts, unemployment benefit enhancements will expire. And that could have big effects on the economy.

rows.title: Federal Officers Could Expand Beyond Portland; Trump Searches For Campaign Strategy
rows.standfirst: In Portland, Oregon, federal agents have been using violent force against protesters. Some protesters have been arrested by officers in unmarked vehicles.

rows.title: BONUS: The Kerner Commission
rows.standfirst: In 1967, President Johnson created a commission to investigate racial unrest in America. But, the answer they came up with was not the answer he was hoping for. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: College Fails
rows.standfirst: The pandemic is transforming college from a can't-miss into a can't-attend experience. Can colleges survive? | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: James Murdoch Quits Family Media Empire News Corp After 'Disagreements'
rows.standfirst: The rupture capped a period of intensifying criticism of coverage and views in the news empire created by his father Rupert Murdoch, such as in The Wall Street Journal and the Fox News Channel.

rows.title: Sharing The Vaccine
rows.standfirst: The biggest, wealthiest nations in the world are in a race to produce a coronavirus vaccine. It's obviously in a country's interest to win that race and protect its citizens. It's also in its interest to share.

rows.title: Microsoft In Talks To Buy TikTok As Trump Threatens A Ban
rows.standfirst: The president's announcement comes as Microsoft is in talks to acquire the app, which is owned by ByteDance, a Chinese company.

rows.title: Florida 17-Year-Old, 'Mastermind' Of Twitter Hack, And Two Others Face Charges
rows.standfirst: In the first criminal charges connected to the Twitter hack earlier this month, state and federal authorities reveal new details about how the scheme allegedly occurred.

rows.title: Facebook Has Moved To Ban Sales Of Looted Antiquities. Will It Make A Difference?
rows.standfirst: Archaeologists have ID'ed 100-plus Facebook groups offering looted and illicit antiquities for sale. New rules ban the sale of "historical artifacts" on Facebook but critics want more enforcement.

rows.title: U.S. Reaches $2.1 Billion Deal With Sanofi, GlaxoSmithKline For COVID-19 Vaccine Push
rows.standfirst: This is the sixth vaccine candidate to join Operation Warp Speed's portfolio, and the largest vaccine deal to date.

rows.title: Members Of The Class Of 2020 Face A Brutal Job Market
rows.standfirst: New college graduates fortunate enough to land jobs during the pandemic begin their careers under bizarre circumstances — they often haven't met their bosses and coworkers in person.

rows.title: GDP -32.9%???!!!
rows.standfirst: This quarter's Gross Domestic Product numbers could be the worst on record. But what do they mean, exactly?

rows.title: Amazon Doubles Profit To $5.2 Billion As Online Shopping Spikes
rows.standfirst: The company's sales went through the roof between April and June, hitting close to $89 billion — a 40% increase from a year earlier. Amazon added 175,000 new hires to help keep up with the demand.

rows.title: Vaccine Candidate Delivers Protection In A Single Shot (In Monkeys)
rows.standfirst: Studies involving COVID-19 vaccine candidates in monkeys show promise of an effective vaccine, but it will take large-scale human trials to know for sure if they work.

rows.title: Germany's Economy Suffers Biggest Quarterly Drop On Record
rows.standfirst: The decline in economic output from March through June was worse than economists expected. Still, the downturn has not inflicted large job losses for Europe's biggest economy.

rows.title: 3 Months Of Hell: U.S. Economy Drops 32.9% In Worst GDP Report Ever
rows.standfirst: The coronavirus triggered the sharpest economic contraction in modern history in the second quarter as the pandemic hammered the economy, the Commerce Department said Thursday.

rows.title: Big-Money Investors Gear Up For A Trillion-Dollar Bet On Farmland
rows.standfirst: A trillion dollars worth of American farmland will change hands in the coming years. Wealthy investors are likely to buy more of it with the power to shape rural communities and the environment.

rows.title: 4 Key Takeaways From Washington's Big Tech Hearing On 'Monopoly Power'
rows.standfirst: Rep. David Cicilline, D-R.I., says Amazon, Facebook, Google and Apple operate like monopolies and need to be broken up or regulated.

frame: Up to15 visible Business-archive cards at four fixed weekly endpoints, restricted to each block; not a full-publication census
